memories.title: Public API backward compatibility window
memories.body: The public API must remain backward compatible for the next two releases. This constraint exists because deployed clients update on a quarterly schedule, and breaking changes would strand those clients.
memories.why: Client update schedules are quarterly and outside the project's control; breaking the API early would strand users.
memories.source_quote: Keep the public API backward compatible for the next two releases. Our deployed clients update quarterly, so breaking the API early would strand those clients.

memories.title: Report Date Formatting Standard
memories.body: Reports must use YYYY-MM-DD (ISO 8601) date format. Slash-formatted dates are prohibited as they cause ambiguity when comparing reports across different regions.
memories.why: User explicitly stated that slash-formatted dates cause ambiguity in cross-region comparisons, requiring a strict ISO format for consistency.
memories.source_quote: Always show dates in YYYY-MM-DD format in reports. I compare reports across regions and slash-formatted dates cause ambiguity.

memories.title: Audit records must be append-only for seven years
memories.body: Audit records must be append-only for seven years because our contractual audit requirements prohibit rewriting historical records.
memories.why: This is a long-lived domain fact and contractual constraint that dictates system architecture (immutable storage) and cannot be derived from code alone.
memories.source_quote: Audit records must be append-only for seven years because our contractual audit requirements prohibit rewriting historical records.
